title: De eximio usu methodi interpolationum in serierum doctrina

deep.reconstruction:
Context: E555 uses Lagrange-type interpolation through infinitely many points to obtain closed forms. Pages 190–191 set up an odd curve y(ω), with abscissa x = θω, through the points (0,0), (±n, ±p), (±(1−n), ±q), (±(1+n), ±r), (±(2−n), ±s), ... in ω-units. The nodes are therefore 0 together with the two interleaved lattices n+ℤ and −n+ℤ.

The Lagrange coefficients are infinite products 𝔄, 𝔅, ℭ, ..., with 𝔅/𝔄, ℭ/𝔄, ... rational in n and ω (p.191). In modern terms the product is
𝔄 = Γ(1−2n)Γ(1+2n) / [Γ(1−n−ω)Γ(1−n+ω)Γ(1+n−ω)Γ(1+n+ω)]
  = 2n·sin π(n+ω)·sin π(n−ω) / [π(n²−ω²)·sin 2πn].

Page 192 assembles the interpolant:
y/(𝔄ω) = p/n − (n²−ω²)q/(n((1−n)²−ω²)) + (n²−ω²)r/(n((1+n)²−ω²)) − ...
Equivalently, ny/(𝔄ω(n²−ω²)) = p/(n²−ω²) − q/((1−n)²−ω²) + r/((1+n)²−ω²) − s/((2−n)²−ω²) + ...
In modern form this is
y(ω) = [2ω·sin π(n+ω)·sin π(n−ω) / (π sin 2πn)] · Σ_k ± p_k/(ω_k²−ω²),
a Lagrange/cardinal-type interpolation series with node function ω·(cos 2πω − cos 2πn). I checked directly that y(n)=p, y(1−n)=q, y(0)=0.

Replacing 𝔄 by Beta integrals gives the prefactor ny/((n−ω)ω)·Δ, with
Δ = ∫z^{n+ω−1}(1−z)^{−n−ω}dz · ∫z^{n+ω−1}(1−z)^{n−ω}dz / ∫z^{n+ω−1}(1−z)^{−2n}dz = 1/((n+ω)𝔄).
All integrals run from 0 to 1. I verified this via Beta/Gamma functions.

§36: the identity 2ω/(a²−ω²) = 1/(a−ω) − 1/(a+ω) splits each term into two. The result is the pair of alternating series for 2nΔy/(n−ω) shown on the page.
§37: the curve has applicates 0, p, q, r, ... at abscissas 0, nθ, (1−n)θ, ..., and is odd.
§38: θ could be set to 1, but is kept for application to circular arcs.
§39 (Scholion): when all |p_k| are equal, the series can be summed using Euler's earlier partial-fraction results:
1/α − 1/(β−α) + 1/(β+α) − ... = π/(β tan(απ/β)), and
1/α + 1/(β−α) − 1/(β+α) − ... = π/(β sin(απ/β)).
Specialising α = n∓ω, β = 1 gives the summations I–IV. I and II are on this page, and both are correct.
errors: None of substance on this page; the formulas check out (Gamma-function verification of Δ = 1/((n+ω)𝔄), the interpolation property, and summations I, II).

Inconsistency with the preceding page: p.191 has the second denominator integral as ∫y^{n+ω−1}(1−y)^{n+ω}dy. The correct factor is (1−y)^{−n−ω}, as printed on p.192. With (1−y)^{n+ω} the Gamma bookkeeping fails; with (1−y)^{−n−ω} it reproduces 𝔄 exactly. This is either a misprint or a transcription error on p.191.

Gap: Euler does not address convergence or uniqueness of the interpolant. One can add any multiple of ω·sin π(n−ω)·sin π(n+ω) times an entire function. Nor does he state growth conditions on p, q, r, ... for the series to converge.
Next page: as transcribed, III and IV are interchanged. The series with signs +,−,+,− equals π/tan((n+ω)π), and the one with +,+,−,− equals π/sin((n+ω)π).

ideas.what: Lagrange interpolation through infinitely many nodes 0, ±n+ℤ. The odd interpolant is written as a partial-fraction series weighted by an infinite-product (sine) node function.
ideas.modern_name: Cardinal/Lagrange interpolation series. Here it is periodic nonuniform (two-coset, 'second-order') sampling expansion with odd symmetry.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whittaker (1915) for the cardinal series; Kohlenberg (1953) and Yen (1956) for second-order / periodic nonuniform sampling; Cauchy and Borel for earlier precursors.
ideas.where_published: E555 itself (Opuscula analytica I, 1783). Earlier interpolation in this paper (§25) treats sine-type data.

ideas.what: Evaluation of the Lagrange normalising infinite product 𝔄 as a quotient of Beta integrals via Euler's product-to-integral rule (§17).
ideas.modern_name: Γ/Beta evaluation of Π(k+a)(k+b)/((k+c)(k+d)) with a+b=c+d
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (Wallis-type products via integrals); Gauss/Weierstrass in Gamma language
ideas.where_published: Euler's papers on infinite products and integrals, e.g. E122 and E321 (unsure of exact numbers); §17 of E555

ideas.what: Partial-fraction expansions of π cot(πα/β) and π csc(πα/β) used to sum the interpolation series in closed form.
ideas.modern_name: Mittag-Leffler expansions of cot and csc
ideas.where_published: Introductio in analysin infinitorum I (1748), ch. X; earlier papers on reciprocal series

missed.claim: Euler's construction is an explicit interpolation (sampling) formula on the nonuniform node set {0}∪(±n+ℤ). This is the two-coset lattice of later 'second-order sampling'. The kernel is the entire function ω·sin π(n−ω)·sin π(n+ω), with Beta-integral normalisation. It anticipates by about 170 years the structure of Kohlenberg/Yen periodic nonuniform sampling formulas. The sampling-theory prehistory literature (Butzer, Stens, Higgins, Ferreira) does not, to my knowledge, cite E555; unsure.
missed.quote: erit per seriem satis concinnam: y/𝔄ω = p/n − (nn−ωω)q/(n((1−n)²−ω²)) + ...
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical priority/precursor point for nonuniform sampling and interpolation of entire functions of exponential type. It is also a clean early example of Lagrange interpolation with a sine-product node function on a shifted double lattice.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a correct, carefully executed infinite Lagrange interpolation on a nonuniform lattice. This is technically routine for Euler, but it is a probably underappreciated precursor of cardinal and second-order sampling series. The paper is published and known, so this is at most a missed-connection/credit issue.
transcription_corrections: First displayed formula: left side should read y/(𝔄ω), not y/(nω).
Integral exponents on this page, (1−z)^{−n−ω} and (1−z)^{n−ω}, are correct. The matching factor on p.191, transcribed as (1−y)^{n+ω}, should be (1−y)^{−n−ω}.
Summation II is correct as π/sin((n−ω)π); the '[?]' can be removed.
